title: One subtraction step
statement: Let $W$ be a word width, let $P$ be a program, and let $m:\mathbb{Z}\to\{0,1\}^W$ be a memory. Suppose the program beginning at position $p$ has a prefix whose first instruction is subtraction of the contents of registers $j$ and $k$ into register $i$, and suppose $m(j)$ and $m(k)$ are the $W$-bit encodings of integers $a$ and $b$. Then one step from position $p$ yields position $p+1$ and memory obtained by replacing register $i$ with the $W$-bit encoding of $a-b$.
hypotheses_covered: The program at position $p$ begins with the specified subtraction instruction
